title: Brahma and the endless stalk
hookLine: the creator god climbs down his lotus stalk looking for where he came from, and never finds the bottom
carry: the source of all has no source
tomorrow: In which forms should I think of you?

cards: At the dawn of a new creation, the Bhagavata Purana says, the old world had dissolved into endless waters, and Vishnu lay resting on them.
From his navel a lotus rose, and on the lotus sat Brahma, the creator god, his four faces looking four ways. And he saw nothing at all. Who am I? he wondered.
Where did this lotus come from? So he climbed down into the hollow stalk, down and down, for ages, looking for its root. He never found the bottom.
At last he climbed back up, sat still, steadied his breath and turned inward. And there, in his own heart, he saw the one he'd been looking for.

teach.h: EVEN THE GODS DON'T KNOW MY ORIGIN.
teach.b: Chapter ten of the Gita opens with the same lesson. Krishna says he'll speak again, because Arjuna delights in hearing.
Verse two: neither the gods nor the great sages know my origin, because I am the origin of the gods and the sages, in every way. That's Brahma in the stalk.

teach.h: I AM THE SOURCE OF ALL.
teach.b: Even the creator can't climb down to the source, because he is downstream of it.
This is one of Hinduism's biggest ideas: one ultimate reality, which the Upanishads call Brahman, behind every god, every being and every thing. In the Gita, Krishna speaks as that source.
Verse eight: I am the source of all; from me everything moves. Then a list that's easy to rush past. Understanding, patience, truth, calm.
Pleasure and pain. Birth and death. Fear and fearlessness.
All these, verse five says, come from me alone.

teach.h: EVEN PAIN AND FEAR, ONE SPRING.
teach.b: Even the hard things share one spring. Verse nine pictures what the wise do: they talk about him together and wake each other up, bodhayantah parasparam.
That's the spirit of satsang, the gathering many Hindus keep to sing and speak of God.
And verse eleven ends where Brahma ended: living in their hearts, out of compassion, I destroy the darkness with the shining lamp of knowledge.
You won't find the source by climbing down. It's found within.

how: Many Hindus hold that one reality, Brahman, is the source of every god and being; many gather for satsang to sing and talk about God, which Gita 10.9 describes as devotees awakening one another, and 10.8 is often recited for its picture of God as the source of all.

o: the first verse of a holy book
the one spring everything flows from
a river's mouth, where it meets the sea

games.q: what's inside the verses — tap the pairs.
p: even the gods don't know my origin
searched the lotus stalk for its root
the lamp of knowledge in the heart

s: the gods know where Krishna came from
verse 2: neither gods nor sages know his origin, because he is theirs.
pain and fear are on the list of what comes from Krishna
verses 4–5 list pleasure and pain, fear and fearlessness, all from him alone.
Brahma found the bottom of the lotus stalk
he searched for ages and never found it; sitting still, he saw the Lord in his own heart (Bhagavata 3.8).

games.q: Brahma can't find the root of his own lotus. by Gita 10.2, why can't even the gods trace Krishna's origin?
o: he is the origin of the gods themselves.
the gods never thought to ask.
games.why: you can't go upstream of the source. the gods and sages come from him, and verse 11 says the light is found in the heart.

practice: Sit still, the way Brahma did when he stopped searching. Follow your breath back as far as you can: the air in the room, the trees and oceans behind it.

Then stop following, and rest your attention at the center of your chest, where verse eleven says the lamp is lit. If you pray, you can hold verse eight in mind: from you, everything moves. If not, simply rest in the quiet.

wordCard.voice: The source. Gita ten, eight: Krishna says he is the origin of all, and from him everything moves. Even Brahma came from it.

orig.note: Sanskrit: prabhava, origin, source; 'aham sarvasya prabhavah', I am the source of all (10.8).

carryVoice: Your line: the source of all has no source. Brahma searched the stalk; the answer was in his heart. See you tomorrow.
